newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: C-C Amatil opens tenth Indonesian plant.
newsitem.headline: C-C Amatil opens tenth Indonesian plant.

text.p: Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd on Wednesday officially opened its tenth bottling plant in Indonesia, built as part of a A$300 milion investment plant.
The A$100 million plant on the outskirts of Jakarta, owned and operated by Coca-Cola Amatil Indonesia, was one of the largest in Asia, C-C Amatil said.
The remaining A$200 million would be spent on marketing and equipment, including refrigeration and transport, a spokesman said.
Coca Cola Amatil Indonesia is owned 90 percent by C-C Amatila and 10 percent by local business interests.
The company has 90 percent of the local carbonated beverages market, but faces strong competition from bottled water, tea and other beverages.
An eleventh Coca Cola bottling plant in Indonesia is operated by an independent bottler.
C-C Amatil is one of the world's largest Coca Cola bottlers, operating in 17 countries in the Asia/Pacific region and Europe.
